minutes.headline: Assessors adopted the data collection manual as a living document and dug into mismatched property record cards after abatements.
minutes.summary: The Board of Assessors heard the interim principal assessor's report, mostly on why the Vision and CAI property cards disagree after the abatement round and what tools the mapping vendor offered. They accepted the data collection manual as a living, dated document, approved two sets of earlier minutes and two sets of executive session minutes, and discussed website improvements, the corrective action request idea, and outreach to seniors. A resident disputed how the lake land values on the 2024 cards were set.

public_comment.topic: Thanked the board for volunteerism, trust and starting the healing process after a hard year; wished everyone a happy holiday season.

Said that for over a hundred abated lake properties the 2024 Vision card land value was inflated by a uniform percentage versus the abated value. Asked for the calculations behind the draft report percentage increases and the sales ratios, and for the ad hoc citizen committees to be formal, open-meeting-law compliant bodies.

what_happened.line: The Board of Assessors accepted the data collection manual as the current version, revised 12/4/2023, to be kept as a living, dated document.
The interim principal assessor reported that the Vision and CAI property cards disagree after the abatement round, and described the mapping vendor's tools.
Review of the property cards was tabled to the next meeting, and the question of when cards are locked or updated goes to the DOR rep.
A senior exemption workshop is to be planned for early March with the senior center and the state rep.
A resident said the 2024 Vision land values on over a hundred abated lake properties exceeded the abated values by a uniform percentage, and asked for the calculations.

why_it_matters: Property cards feed each owner's assessed value and abatement outcome, so mismatches between the two record systems can bear on how a bill is set or appealed.
Lake property owners and seniors have a stated next step: a request for the calculations behind the draft revaluation percentages, and a March exemption workshop.
watch_next: The next Board of Assessors meeting, where the tabled property card review and the deferred October 11 and November 20 minutes are due.
A Zoom Q&A with the vendor contact, likely in January, and the early-March senior exemption workshop.
